title: Class Imbalance Mitigation Strategies
description: Remediation techniques for severe classification target skewness (e.g. positive class < 5%).
conditions: Binary or multiclass classification where minority class prevalence is < 10% (fraud, disease, rare failure)
Model predicts only the majority class while achieving misleadingly high accuracy
recommended_methods: Algorithmic cost-sensitive weighting (class_weight='balanced' or scale_pos_weight in XGBoost)
Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) applied strictly to training folds
Post-hoc classification threshold tuning optimizing F1-Score or Cost Utility Matrix
selection_rules: Never evaluate an imbalanced classifier using Raw Accuracy; evaluate PR-AUC (Precision-Recall AUC) and Balanced Accuracy
Prefer cost-sensitive class weighting over SMOTE; weighting does not synthesize noisy artificial examples
Tune decision threshold away from default 0.50 based on business cost ratio of False Positives vs False Negatives
limitations: SMOTE creates synthetic samples in feature space that can bridge across class boundaries in noisy data
Extreme oversampling drastically increases training time
source: Chawla et al. (2002) SMOTE: Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique
